svg.title: The Bill of Sale: partition of Irad in the 2007 drafts
svg.desc: How the draft treaties negotiated by the government of the Democratic Republic of Irad in December 2006 – February 2007 would have divided Irad. Kazakhstan: the northern steppe, the lower Chu with Nurzhan and the lands next to its Turkistan and Jambyl regions (about 170,100 km²). Kyrgyzstan: the Talas valley with the capital and the Chatkal, Toktogul and Naryn lands next to its Jalal-Abad region (about 36,300 km²). Uzbekistan: the Fergana rim (about 12,000 km²). The new boundaries follow the neighbours' own internal boundaries, except on the Fergana rim. Base map and boundaries: Natural Earth (public domain); Irad's border and places: Kartalar map data; relief: SRTM via the AWS Terrain Tiles (public domain). Chu, Talas and Chatkal rivers © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

g.text: Boundaries as described in the drafts.
